result.summary: Extracts logic for nine P2P message types out of the monolithic `PeerManagerImpl::ProcessMessage()` into dedicated member functions in `src/net_processing.cpp`. Each message handler is extracted in its own move-only commit, followed by a final commit normalizing formatting and control flow.
result.problem: `PeerManagerImpl::ProcessMessage()` is an oversized (~1,000-line) function that handles every P2P message type inline, making navigation, scoping, and review in `net_processing` difficult.
evidence: Author notes the extraction continues the pattern of merged PR commits fa5ab0220e02377c3c855042ecdf1f5f950d0965 (ProcessPong) and fa55723b8fbd4fd056dddac5b35daf2e86021422 (ProcessAddrs), suggested in #34588.
result.scope_notes: The PR consists of nine move-only extraction commits designed to be reviewed with `--color-moved=dimmed-zebra --color-moved-ws=ignore-all-space`, followed by one commit containing minor formatting cleanups and control flow adjustments.
result.changed_since_previous: Rebased with minor co-author metadata additions and updated commit hashes while preserving the same structure and message extractions.
result.card: Extracts handling logic for nine P2P message types out of `PeerManagerImpl::ProcessMessage()` in `src/net_processing.cpp` into dedicated helper functions across nine move-only commits and one cleanup commit. The function is an oversized monolith handling many message types inline, making navigation and code maintenance in `net_processing` cumbersome. The author notes this continues previously merged cleanup work splitting up the ~1,000-line function. It makes no intentional functional changes aside from a function name in one debug log.

risk.why: A mistake in control flow or lock annotations while moving message-processing logic could disconnect peers, drop P2P messages, or crash nodes.
